cases.input: Migra una búsqueda de nombres Unicode con collation Turkish_CI_AS de SQL Server a PostgreSQL sin extensiones. Declara si no puedes garantizar igual semántica para cualquier cadena. Rutina migration.search_names, parámetros p_name text; salida name text.

output.code:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION migration.search_names(p_name text)
RETURNS TABLE(name text)
LANGUAGE sql
SECURITY INVOKER
AS $func$
-- This implements a Turkish-aware case-insensitive equality search without extensions.
-- It applies a small, explicit Turkish case mapping for dotted/dotless I before using lower().
-- It selects from domain.names (expects domain.names(name text) to exist in the database).
SELECT n.name
FROM domain.names n
WHERE (
  -- apply Turkish-specific mapping to stored name and input, then compare for equality
  lower(replace(replace(n.name, 'İ', 'i'), 'I', 'ı'))
  =
  lower(replace(replace(p_name, 'İ', 'i'), 'I', 'ı'))
);
$func$;
semantic_differences: PostgreSQL collation and comparison are not identical to SQL Server Turkish_CI_AS; this function approximates Turkish case-insensitive matching only by performing an explicit mapping for the dotted/dotless I (U+0130, U+0049 -> U+0069, U+0131) prior to applying lower().

This routine does not reproduce full SQL Server Turkish_CI_AS collation ordering (sorting) semantics; it only attempts to replicate case-insensitive equality comparison for many common Latin Turkish characters.

Unicode case folding beyond the handled dotted/dotless I mappings (for example, combining marks, locale-dependent mappings for other characters, or complex multi-codepoint mappings) is not fully reproduced. Strings containing such cases may compare differently than under Turkish_CI_AS.
This implementation treats NULLs according to SQL semantics: comparisons with NULL do not match. If the original T-SQL relied on different NULL handling, results will differ.
If the original search used pattern matching (LIKE) or different comparison operators, this implementation provides exact equality only. Pattern/substring behavior is not implemented here.
Rounding, numeric, and date behaviors are not applicable to this routine; no changes made.
output.explanation: This provides a single-schema migration routine migration.search_names(p_name text) returning name text. It queries domain.names(name text) and implements Turkish-aware case-insensitive equality by first replacing the Turkish dotted/dotless I characters (İ -> i, I -> ı) and then calling lower() on both sides. Exact SQL Server Turkish_CI_AS collation cannot be fully reproduced in PostgreSQL without ICU collations or extensions; therefore the function approximates only the key Turkish case mappings. The function is in SQL language and SECURITY INVOKER as required. The adaptation is an explicit SELECT returning the result set; if the original T-SQL used EXEC/OUTPUT, call the function with SELECT * FROM migration.search_names(p_name) to obtain the same columns.

cases.input: Migra exactamente lectura concurrente SELECT * FROM dbo.policies WITH (NOLOCK) a PostgreSQL. No puedes cambiar niveles de aislamiento. Rutina migration.read_policies, sin parámetros, salida id integer. Declara si no es representable con igual semántica.

output.code:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION migration.read_policies()
RETURNS TABLE(id integer)
LANGUAGE sql
SECURITY INVOKER
AS $$
  -- Original T-SQL: SELECT * FROM dbo.policies WITH (NOLOCK)
  -- PostgreSQL has no NOLOCK hint. Return the id column as requested.
  SELECT id FROM dbo.policies;
$$;
semantic_differences: SQL Server hint WITH (NOLOCK) allows reading uncommitted (dirty) rows (approx. READ UNCOMMITTED). PostgreSQL does not support a NOLOCK equivalent; its minimum isolation behavior is effectively READ COMMITTED (dirty reads are not allowed). This function does not reproduce dirty/partial/phantom reads that NOLOCK can return in SQL Server.

Because the task forbids changing transaction isolation levels, the routine does not and cannot alter session or transaction isolation to attempt to emulate NOLOCK. Therefore identical concurrency/visibility semantics under concurrent writers are not representable.

Any reliance in caller code on NOLOCK-specific behavior (seeing in-flight uncommitted changes, reading rows while they are being modified, or observing torn/partially-written multi-column updates) will not be reproduced by this PostgreSQL function.
output.explanation: This is a direct migration of the T-SQL SELECT * FROM dbo.policies WITH (NOLOCK) into a PostgreSQL routine migration.read_policies() returning only the requested id column. PostgreSQL does not implement table hints like WITH (NOLOCK). The closest SQL Server semantics (READ UNCOMMITTED / dirty reads) cannot be reproduced without changing the transaction isolation level or using non-portable server extensions; the task explicitly forbids changing isolation levels, so the function issues a plain SELECT against dbo.policies. The consequence is a semantic difference in concurrent read behavior: this routine will not return the dirty/uncommitted values that NOLOCK may expose in SQL Server. The function preserves column naming and returns exactly the declared column set (id integer).
